DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Phiiippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO JAN 3 1 2025 MS. NINA A1-VIAR alviarl 32gmail.com Dear Ms. Aiviar: This refers to your request via email requesting for this Department's legal opinion as regards the "residency" requirement under Section 471 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), which states that "no person shall be appointed assistant treasurer unless he is a resident of the local government unit concerned". Specifically, you want to be clarified on whether a person who is a registered voter of an LGU, but does not not permanently reside therein, is considered a resident of that LGU. With regret, this Department cannot render the opinion requested. At the outset, pursuant to Memorandum Order 2010-02, the Department consistently refrains from rendering an opinion or gives legal advice on queries that are cognizable by other agencies or offices of the government, in this case the Civil Service Commission (CSC) over which we possess no supervisory or revisory authority. The underlying considerations apropos this policy are respect and deference to the competence and expertise of the office having primary consideration to resolve the matter as well as recognition of the lawful exercise of an authority conferred by law. It appears that your concern relates to the qualification standards for "appointment" to the position of "Assistant Treasurer", which falls within the mandate of the Civil Service Commission (CSC) as the "central personnel agencyl" of the Philippine govemment. While the query requires a legal interpretation of a provision of law (Sec. 471) which is essentially a judicial function, it is an established rule in administrative law that the administrave agency that manages or enforces the subject law or rule is in a better position to interpret the ambiguous provisions of the law or rule that deal with administrative action. Hence, it is the CSC that has the primary authority to issue legal advisories or opinions on the matter of the qualification standards for local fiscal officers. It is, thus, recommended to refer the matter to that office for clarification and/or opinion. Nonetheless, for your information and guidance, we provide the following discussion. I Section 3, Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

The provisions of Section 471 of Republic Act No. 7160, or the Local Government Code of 1991 (hereinafter the "Code'), which sets out the minimum qualifications for assistant treasurers in the LGU , thus: Section 471. Assistant Treasurer. a) An assistant treasurer may be appointed by the Secretary of Finance from a list of at least three (3) ranking, eligible recommendees of the governor or mayor, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. b) No person shall be appointed assistant treasurer unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government unit concerned, of good moral character, a holder of a college degree preferably in commerce, public administration, or law from a recognized college or university, and a first grade civil service eligible or its equivalent. He must have acquired at least five (5) years experience in the treasury or accounting service in the case of the city or provincial assistant treasurer and three (3) years in the case of municipal assistant treasurer. The appointment of an assistant treasurer shall be optional for provincial, city and municipal governments; As can be deduced from Sec. 471, an Assistant Treasurer may be appointed by the Secretary of Finance from a list of eligible recommendees of the Mayor. Note that the appointment of an Assistant Treasurer of an LGU is optional. Nonetheless, whenever a recommendation for appointment to the posion of Assistant Treasurer is issued by the Local Chief Executive Officer, e.g. City Mayor, the recommendee satisfy the following requirements: (1) must be a citizen of the Philippines; (2) must be a resident of the local government unit concerned; (3) must have good moral character;(4) must be a college degree holder in the field of commerce, public administration, or law; (5) must be at least a first grade civil service eligible or its equivalent; and (6) must have acquired at least 5 years working experience in treasury or accounting services in the case of the city or provincial assistant treasurer and three (3) years in the case of municipal assistant treasurer. As regards the "residency" qualification, we cite the case of Marcos vs. COMELEC2 where the Supreme Court had the occasion to explain the concept of the term "residence", thus: Residence. in its ordinary conception. implies the factual relationship of an individual to a certain place. It is the physical presence of a person in a given area. community or country. The essential distinction between residence and domicile in law is that residence involves the intent to leave when the purpose for which the resident has taken up his abode ends. One may seek a place for purposes such as pleasure, business, or health. If a person's intent be to remain, it becomes his domicile; if his intent is to leave as soon as his purpose is established it is residence. It is thus. quite perfectly normal for an individual to have different residences in various places. However, a person can only have a single domicile, unless, for various reasons, he successfully abandons his domicile in favor of another domicile of choice. 2 G.R. No. 119976 September 18, 1995 Page 2 of 2

From the foregoing, it is our considered view that voter registration does not necessarily equate to residency if the individual does not demonstrate physical presence there. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, it is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY SECRETARY ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/JVRL/LLLS-LRALLD/jvpr Page 2 of 2
